newsitem.title: FRANCE: PSA Peugeot 97 first-half sales rise 6.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: PSA Peugeot 97 first-half sales rise 6.3 pct.

text.p: French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen said on Wednesday first-half turnover rose 6.3 percent to 94.64 billion francs, bolstered by brisk sales of its new light commercial vehicles and a surge in exports of cars and car parts.
In volume terms, sales rose faster, climbing seven percent over the first half of 1996 to 1,094,400 units.
The figures showed a slight drop in turnover per vehicle due to a fierce price war being fought in the European market.

The Peugeot group said the success of the new Citroen Berlingo and Peugeot Partner light vans and a 41 percent jump in export volumes more than offset a weak performance in Europe and a poor showing in the collapsing French market.
PSA's car sales in Europe fell 5.1 percent to 761,000 units due to a 23.7 percent slide in the French car market after the expiry of a state car buying incentive programme.
In Europe excluding France, the Peugeot group's car sales rose 9.9 percent to 535,300 units.
Its total car sales rose 4.3 percent, but sales of light commercial vehicles jumped 28.3 percent in the six months to June 30.
The company said it benefited from currency movements, notably sterling's rise in the first half of 1997, but said the currency gains were offset by a deterioration in product and geographic mix.
With the Spanish and Italian markets showing the fastest growth fuelled by buying incentives, the proportion of Peugeot and Citroen vehicles sold in markets with weaker currencies increased.
The company also sold a higher proportion of small cars, which fetch lower prices than large cars.
